commands.name: completion
commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for symdesk for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

commands.name: bash
commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for bash
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(symdesk completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	symdesk completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/symdesk

#### macOS:

	symdesk completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/symdesk

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

commands.name: fish
commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for fish
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	symdesk completion fish | source

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

	symdesk completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/symdesk.fish

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

commands.name: powershell
commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for powershell
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	symdesk completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression

To load completions for every new session, add the output of the above command
to your powershell profile.

commands.name: zsh
commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for zsh
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(symdesk completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	symdesk completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_symdesk"

#### macOS:

	symdesk completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_symdesk

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

commands.short: Paperless-ngx migration tools

commands.name: import
commands.short: Import documents from a Paperless-ngx export into the vault
commands.long:
Read a Paperless-ngx export directory (manifest.json + document files) and
create or update contract-v2 notes in the vault. The import is idempotent:
re-running against the same export will update existing notes rather than
creating duplicates, keyed on the Paperless document ID and checksum.

Each document is placed in paperless/ with its original file archived in
archive/paperless/. Metadata — correspondents, document types, tags, ASN,
document date — is preserved in the note frontmatter.

local_flags.name: dry-run
local_flags.usage: report what would happen without making changes

commands.name: migrate
commands.short: Import documents from a Paperless-ngx instance via its API
commands.long:
Connect to a running Paperless-ngx instance (--base-url + --token) and
import its documents into the vault, running them through the symingest OCR
pipeline and writing Markdown + YAML frontmatter notes. Idempotent: re-running
updates existing notes keyed on the Paperless document ID and checksum.

commands.name: transform
commands.short: Transform text with AI (summarize|rewrite|continue); reads text from --text or stdin
commands.long: Transform a piece of text with a local AI action. The intent is one of summarize, rewrite or continue. The text is taken from --text, or read from stdin when the flag is empty. Operates purely on the given text and never touches the vault; degrades honestly when Ollama is not configured.

commands.name: adopt
commands.short: Bring an existing Markdown or Obsidian vault up to the contract in place
commands.long:
Scan an existing Markdown vault and backfill required frontmatter fields
(title, created, tags) in place. Existing frontmatter keys and unknown fields
are preserved byte-for-byte. Pre-adoption versions are captured in the version
history safety net (.symdesk/history/) before any file is written.
